target.title: fix(agent-tools): add request timeout to remote media fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The image, image-generate, and PDF agent tools load remote media through `loadWebMedia` / `loadWebMediaRaw`, which only exposed `readIdleTimeoutMs` (idle timeout between data chunks). A remote endpoint that accepts the connection then never sends headers - or withholds response data - held the tool's media load open indefinitely, blocking the agent run.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR applies the shared bounded-media total-request lifetime to the three agent-tool remote-media callers via a new `REMOTE_MEDIA_TIMEOUT_MS` constant, forwarded through the `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs` seam (the shared API candidate in canonical PR #103206).

The total deadline is `15 * 60_000` (15 min), **aligning with the canonical bounded-media ceiling** established by the merged node-camera fix (#103266). ClawSweeper flagged the earlier 120 s value as a P1 compatibility risk because `timeoutMs` stays active through complete body consumption and would newly fail slow-but-progressing transfers (image/PDF); 15 min matches the accepted precedent while `REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (120 s) continues to bound body-idle stalls on a tighter schedule.

**Landing boundary:** this fork cross-repo PR includes the `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs` seam so it typechecks and stays green on its own; it reduces to agent-tool-only once the canonical seam+Tlon PR #103206 lands. The Tlon caller changes live in #103206; the earlier Tlon-only #103199 is closed as a subset.

## User Impact

- Agent-tool remote media fetches (reference images, URL-backed PDFs) that previously hung forever on a never-responding endpoint now abort after the total deadline and surface a fetch error instead of stalling the run.
- Slow-but-progressing transfers are unaffected: they remain bounded by `REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, and 15 min is the accepted ceiling for legitimate large transfers.

## Evidence

**Source:**
- `src/agents/tools/media-tool-shared.ts`: `export const REMOTE_MEDIA_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`, `image-generate-tool.ts`, `pdf-tool.ts`: pass `timeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_TIMEOUT_MS` on remote (`isHttpUrl`) loads.
- `src/media/web-media.ts`: forward `timeoutMs` through `loadWebMediaInternal` to `readRemoteMediaBuffer` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard`'s abort signal (shared seam; see #103206).

**Tests (focused suite, run locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`; Crabbox unavailable in this environment so the allowed local fallback was used):**
- `image-tool.test.ts`, `image-generate-tool.test.ts`, `pdf-tool.test.ts`: assert `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000` is forwarded on remote loads (alongside the existing `readIdleTimeoutMs` assertions).
- The shared `timeoutMs` abort behavior (never-responding endpoint -> abort at the deadline) is proven in #103206's `web-media.test.ts` stalled-endpoint test, and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`'s `timeoutMs` -> `fetchWithSsrFGuard` abort-signal forwarding is covered by `src/media/fetch.test.ts`.

**Proof transcript (redacted):**
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3) | Tests 180 passed (180)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ createPdfTool > passes web_fetch SSRF policy when loading remote PDFs
 ✓ createPdfTool > passes the shared remote read idle timeout when loading remote PDFs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ createImageGenerateTool > passes web_fetch SSRF policy to remote reference images
```

Change: +38 / -3 across 8 files (5 source, 3 tests).
